title: P3D Slicer – Robot 3D Printing Software
excerpt: P3D Slicer and ENCY for multi-axis robot 3D printing, large-scale additive manufacturing and hybrid processes.
content:
🇩🇪 Deutsch   🇬🇧 English

3D Printing with up to 8 Axes

Complex 3D freeform surfaces and simultaneous multi-axis printing for demanding industrial additive manufacturing applications.

P3D Slicer at a Glance

1. Import 3D CAD

Import STL or STEP files as individual parts or assemblies.

2. Simulation

Toolpath and feed simulation.

3. NC Output

NC output for industrial robots and CNC machines, including KUKA, ABB, Stäubli, Yaskawa, FANUC, DMG and Hermle.

4. Support for Extruders

Support for pellet, filament and other extrusion systems, enabling the processing of a broad range of materials, including composites, metals and casting materials.

BMW Project – Center Console Support

Printing time: less than 3 hours. ABB and KUKA robots.

Large-Scale 3D Printing

1. Larger Components

Large-scale printing enables large objects to be manufactured in a single printing process.

2. Cost Efficiency

Robot-based 3D printing can reduce material costs and production times.

3. Design Flexibility

Large build areas offer greater design freedom for innovative and complex structures.

4. Adaptability

Robots can be configured for different printing requirements and materials.

Hybrid Manufacturing

Discover the future of manufacturing with our integrated system. P3D and ENCY combine printing, milling, cutting, welding and part placement in a single powerful system. Benefit from seamless processes and improved production efficiency. Contact us for further information.

Customer Perspective

What makes our P3D robot printing process in combination with ENCY special?

With P3D, we have achieved a quantum leap in 3D printing. Combining the flexibility of a multi-axis robot with precision and the ability to integrate printing and milling in one system is truly groundbreaking.

Andreas Reitz, Managing Director, Datentechnik Reitz GmbH & Co. KG

Component Size

The size of the components is limited primarily by the robot's working envelope. The component shown is over 2 meters long and 1 meter high. Printing took approximately 8 hours.

Maximum Freedom of Movement

Supported systems provide extensive flexibility in reaching different areas. Rotary and tilting tables are supported in addition to the robot axes.

Printing on Existing Surfaces

Printing on previously prepared surfaces—or preparing those surfaces with a milling module on the same system—opens up a wide range of possibilities.

Controlling the Fourth and Fifth Axes

Additional axes enable the processing of complex non-planar components while helping to avoid unfavorable printing orientations.

Applications

Prototyping

Prototyping often involves one-off production, making our process particularly suitable.

Mold and Model Making

Model and mold making remain major applications for 3D printing, allowing prototypes to be produced efficiently.

Medical Technology

Complex shapes and models are needed in medical applications. Almost any contour can now be printed, including in color.

Advertising and Signage

Signs, lettering and other advertising elements can be printed in a wide range of sizes.

Scientific Models

Physical scientific models for education and training.

Architecture

Complete architectural models can be printed using our software and hardware solutions.

Set Design and Art

Artistic objects and stage sets are ideal applications for robot-based 3D printing.

Landscape Design

3D printing can realistically reproduce landscape and urban planning models.

Exhibition Stand Construction

Our large-scale 3D printing systems support the design and production of exhibition stands, including entire walls.

Restoration

Whether restoring vehicles, historical buildings or individual components, our robot printing solutions provide flexible manufacturing options.

Layer-by-Layer Printing

In this established process, material is deposited layer by layer from the bottom up.

Limitation: visible stair-step effects can impair surface quality, particularly in shallow concave areas.

Freeform Printing

Our software supports freeform printing, which can generate smoother surfaces without pronounced stair-step effects.

Limitation: the nozzle distance may vary along the component cross-section and become too large in certain areas.

Simultaneous 5-Axis Printing

ENCY supports this method, as do our CENTUM 3D printers. The nozzle is guided around the component using five axes, maintaining a consistent nozzle distance.

Limitation: gravity restricts how far the nozzle can be tilted.

8-Axis Printing

With ENCY and CENTUM, simultaneous 8-axis printing is possible: six robot axes plus two rotary axes. This enables the nozzle to maintain the correct distance and orientation relative to the component. The original German page describes this process as having no disadvantages.
